inline.s: Question: Why did he not have one practise contemplation (referring to the thirteen contemplations in the Sutra on Contemplation of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, such as the contemplation of the sun and of the water), but directly teach exclusive recitation of the name? Answer: Because the karmic hindrances of sentient beings are deep and heavy, the objects of contemplation (the objects contemplated) are subtle while the mind is coarse, the consciousness is agitated and the spirit flies, so practising contemplation is hard to accomplish. Therefore Shakyamuni Buddha, in compassion, directly teaches exclusive recitation of Amitabha Buddha's name. Precisely because reciting the name is easy, as long as the thought of recitation continues thought after thought, one at once attains rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. If one's thought of recitation continues thought after thought, one who practises thus for one's whole life, of ten people ten are reborn, of a hundred a hundred are reborn. Why? Because exclusive recitation of the name means the mind does not reach outward (the mind does not cling to external objects), and thus one attains right mindfulness; because it accords with Amitabha Buddha's primal vow, because it does not violate Shakyamuni Buddha's teaching, because it follows Shakyamuni Buddha's holy words.

Xiangxu ji sheng (being continuous, one is at once reborn): 'being continuous, one is at once reborn' means that the thought of recitation continues thought after thought, and at the end of life one at once attains rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. Here 'continuous' is the 'pure thought continuous' spoken of in the Chapter on the Perfect Penetration of Reciting the Buddha by the Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta, that is, the thought of recitation continuing thought after thought, with no false thought mixed in the midst (if a false thought is mixed in, it is not continuity), and this is the state of single-minded, undistracted concentration (the state of the mind bound and not scattered). One must never misunderstand the two words 'continuous' here as the continuation of the name on the lips (while false thoughts are mixed in the mind). As the saying goes, a hair's breadth of error leads to a thousand leagues of mistake.

If one abandons exclusive recitation and cultivates miscellaneous karma, of a hundred one rarely gets one or two, of a thousand one rarely gets three or four. Why? Because mixed conditions stir things up and one loses right mindfulness; because it does not accord with the Buddha's primal vow, because it violates the teaching, because it does not follow the Buddha's words, because the binding of thought is not continuous, because the mind is not continuously mindful of the Buddha's grace, because though one does deeds of karma they are ever tied to fame and profit, because one delights in approaching mixed conditions, hindering oneself and hindering others' correct practice of rebirth.

If one abandons the single-minded, attentive recitation of Amitabha Buddha's name and cultivates miscellaneous karma, of a hundred people it is rare to find one or two reborn, of a thousand it is rare to find three or four reborn. Why? Because mixed conditions stir things up and one loses right mindfulness; because it does not accord with Amitabha Buddha's primal vow; because it violates Shakyamuni Buddha's teaching; because it does not follow Shakyamuni Buddha's holy words; because the binding of thought is not continuous; because the mind is not continuously mindful to repay the Buddha's grace; because though one does all kinds of karmic deeds, they are ever tied to fame and profit; because one delights in approaching mixed conditions, hindering oneself (obstructing oneself) and hindering others (obstructing others) in the correct practice of rebirth.

I wish all people to reflect well: whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one must rouse the mind and restrain oneself, day and night never give up; when the previous thought ends this life, the next thought is already reborn, forever enjoying the unconditioned bliss of Dharma, and even attaining Buddhahood, how delightful!
I wish
all people
to reflect well: whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down,
all
must rouse the mind and restrain themselves, day and night never giving up.
Practising thus,
when the previous thought ends this life, the next thought is born in
the Western Land of Utmost Bliss,
forever enjoying the unconditioned bliss of Dharma, and even attaining Buddhahood, how delightful!

Qian nian mingzhong, hou nian ji sheng (when the previous thought ends this life, the next thought is at once reborn): this is to say that, because the recitation continues thought after thought, the very last thought at death is necessarily a thought of the Buddha's name, and
after that last thought
one is immediately reborn in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss.
The following teaching is taken from Master Shandao's Essay on Right Mindfulness at Death and Rebirth. Whether rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss requires right mindfulness at death,
this is the dividing line between the right and the wrong teachings of the Pure Land school.

The right teaching follows the meaning of the scriptures and affirms that right mindfulness at death is required; thus Master Shandao taught 'being continuous, one is at once reborn.' Master Yongming taught 'the ten recitations at death are accomplished.' Master Lianchi taught 'within, concentrate right mindfulness; without, move the Buddha to come welcome.' The wrong teaching, however, violates the meaning of the scriptures, denies that right mindfulness at death is required, and advocates 'reciting the name surely attains rebirth.'
Master Shandao's Essay on Right Mindfulness at Death and Rebirth (for the full text see
Master Shandao's Essay on Right Mindfulness at Death and Rebirth

) causes the claim 'reciting the name surely attains rebirth' to collapse on its own; therefore the Collected Works of Master Shandao compiled by Master Huijing and Master Jingzong and published by the Pure Land Publishing House in
deleted this Essay on Right Mindfulness at Death and Rebirth.
From this one can see the intentions of Honen's followers! Tell me, is this how you rely on Master Shandao? Is this how you inherit and propagate Master Shandao's Pure Land thought?
Moreover, in the Four-Volume Commentary on the Sutra on Contemplation, Master Shandao explained the meaning of the chapter on the lowest rebirth, saying:

“'From this foolish person' down to 'the offenses of birth-and-death,' it clearly shows that hearing the Dharma and reciting the Buddha gets the present benefit, in ten points: first, it shows again the person who has done evil; second, it shows his life is extended but brief; third, it shows meeting a good friend at death; fourth, it shows the good person comforts and teaches him to recite the Buddha; fifth, it shows the suffering of death pressing the offender, leaving no way to recite the Buddha's name; sixth, it shows the good friend, knowing his suffering and his failing mindfulness, instead teaches him to recite aloud the name of Amitabha Buddha; seventh, it shows how many recitations, each sound unbroken; eighth, it shows the removal of offenses of many aeons; ninth,
it shows that right mindfulness at death means the golden lotus comes to respond;
tenth, it shows the speed of his going, straight to the land he is destined for.”
Please pay special attention: here Master Shandao says:
right mindfulness at death and rebirth
('it shows that right mindfulness at death means the golden lotus comes to respond'). (See
Commentary on the Chapter on the Lowest Rebirth in the Sutra on Contemplation
article.) Yet the Primal Vow school, which claims aloud to 'rely on Master Shandao,' resolutely opposes rebirth through right mindfulness at death!

When one is gravely ill and about to die, the relatives must not shed tears and weep, nor make sounds of sighing and regret, disturbing the mind and spirit and causing him to lose right mindfulness. But all together with one voice recite the Buddha's name, and only after his breath is finished may they lament. If he has the slightest thought of clinging to this world, it becomes an impediment, and he cannot gain liberation. If one obtains a person who understands the Pure Land to come frequently and encourage him, this is extremely fortunate. If one follows this, he will certainly be reborn, without any doubt.

If one is gravely ill and about to die, the relatives must not shed tears and weep, nor make sounds of sighing and regret, lest they disturb the mind and spirit of the patient and cause him to lose right mindfulness. Instead they must recite the Buddha's name in unison, and only after the patient's breath has ended may they lament. For if the patient has the slightest thought of clinging to this world, it becomes an impediment to his rebirth, and he cannot gain liberation. If one can have a person who understands the Pure Land come frequently to encourage him, this is a great blessing. If one acts according to this, the patient will certainly be reborn in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, without any doubt.

This method, used by monks, lay people, and even those who have never recited the Buddha's name, all attain rebirth, without any doubt. I have often seen worldly people who in daily life recite the Buddha and praise, vowing to seek rebirth in the West, very earnest
(sincere and genuine).

But when it comes to illness, they again fear death, and never speak of the matter of rebirth and liberation. Only when their breath fades and life ends, and their consciousness passes into the netherworld, do they begin the ten recitations. Just like shutting the door after the thief has gone, what use is it? Life and death are great matters; one must make the effort oneself. If one thought goes wrong, one suffers for aeons; who can take one's place? Think on this! Think on this! When one has nothing to do, one should take this method and practise it diligently, for this is the great matter at death.

This method of 'right mindfulness at death and rebirth' (the patient should try his utmost to maintain right mindfulness at death; the relatives must not weep and sigh lest they disturb the patient's right mindfulness at death; and the timely guidance and encouragement of a good friend can help the patient raise and maintain right mindfulness at death), used by monks, lay people, and even those who have never recited the Buddha's name, all attain rebirth, without any doubt. I have seen many people in the world who in daily life recite the Buddha and praise, vowing to seek rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, very sincere and genuine. But when they fall ill, they again fear death and speak not at all of the matter of rebirth and liberation. Only when their own breath fades and life ends, and their consciousness enters the netherworld, do they begin to recite the Buddha in ten thoughts. This is exactly like shutting the door after the thief has gone (the thief has already stolen the goods before one shuts the door to guard against him), what use is it? Life and death are great matters; one must diligently apply oneself.
If one thought goes wrong, one suffers for aeons;
who can take one's place?
Think on this! Think on this!

Before one falls ill, one should take this method of 'right mindfulness at death and rebirth' and practise it diligently (one should make full preparation for right mindfulness at death, which is what Master Yongming called 'preparing the ferry beforehand'; at the same time warn the relatives not to weep and sigh at that time, and it is even better to have the deathbed help of a good friend), for this is the great matter at death!

blocks.text: The Characteristics of the Wrong Teaching

inline.s: Question: On the practice of the Pure Land school there are many conflicting claims; some even say that the true Pure Land requires no practice. Which is right and which is wrong, and how should one distinguish?

Answer: The claim that the Pure Land school requires no practice is quite wrong. At the end of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life spoken by the Buddha, the Buddha earnestly said: 'You should believe and follow,
and practise according to the Dharma.'
In the Sutra Praising the Pure Land and Its Buddha's Reception, the Buddha again and again earnestly said: '
practise as it is spoken.'

As for how to distinguish whether the various claims about the practice of the Pure Land school are right or wrong, one should judge according to the principle of 'rely on the Dharma, not on the person.' What accords with the words and meaning of the scriptures is right; what is contrary is wrong. Grand talk that cites no scriptures is indeed untrustworthy; but even when one cites scriptures or the teachings of the patriarchs, one must also note whether it is taking passages out of context or twisting the scriptures or the patriarchs' original words (the example just given, 'Honen's fabrication of the gate of the extensive vow,' is one such case).

In general, the wrong teaching has the following characteristics. First: it does not cite the scriptures, but fabricates out of thin air and makes things up. Second: it winds around, going east and west, round and round, so that people cannot tell what is spoken by the Buddha and what is spoken by a person, and they take a fallacy for the truth. Third: when it cites the scriptures, it takes passages out of context and twists them. Fourth: it says such and such a sutra says thus and so, but does not attach the original text. If you carefully look up the original text, either you cannot find it at all in the sutra they mention, or the corresponding text has already been deliberately altered by them. Observe these characteristics carefully and you will find them.
The Sutra Praising the Pure Land and Its Buddha's Reception is the '
Dharma-gate received by all the Buddhas
praised by the Buddhas of the ten directions, of course including Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. In it the Buddha said:

“Sariputra, in this West there are also the Tathagata of Immeasurable Life, the Tathagata of Immeasurable Aggregates, the Tathagata of Immeasurable Light, the Tathagata of Immeasurable Banner, the Tathagata of Great Freedom, the Tathagata of Great Light, the Tathagata of Flaming Light, the Tathagata of the Great Jewel Banner, the Tathagata of Emitting Light, and Buddhas such as these, like the sands of the Ganges, dwelling in their own Buddhalands in the West. Each displays the vast tongue, covering the whole three-thousand great-thousand world all around, and speaks true words: you sentient beings, all should faithfully receive this 'praise of the inconceivable merit of the Buddhaland, the '
Dharma-gate received by all the Buddhas

Therefore students of the Pure Land should practise respectfully according to the teaching; what accords with the words and meaning of this Sutra Praising the Pure Land and Its Buddha's Reception is right, and what is contrary is wrong.

blocks.text: The True Pure Land and the False Pure Land

inline.s: Question: Some now say that certain people are impure Pure Land and certain are false Pure Land, and that they alone are the true Pure Land. How should one judge?

Answer: The so-called 'impure Pure Land' is the language of people who are arrogant, praising themselves and disparaging others, so we do not adopt it. As for who is the true Pure Land and who is the false Pure Land, we let the facts speak and history bear witness (see
The Primal Vow School Is an Attachment-Buddha External Path
To Honen's followers (Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others), we address a few plain words:

If you yourselves wish to revere Japan's Master Honen as the patriarch, that is your own affair; but you must not place Honen, who has not even attained single-mindedness, above the patriarchs of our country's Pure Land school who realized the pratyutpanna samadhi and the samadhi of reciting the Buddha,
and even slander them as impure, without lineage, and so on.
Be it known that
Master Yongming, the manifestation of Amitabha Buddha
came to our country earlier than the time when Japan's Master Honen
was born.

And he left behind the hundred-fascicle Record of the Mirror of the Source and the six-fascicle Collected All-Good Return of Myriad Good Deeds, giving a comprehensive exposition of the whole Buddha-Dharma (of course including the Pure Land); and to clarify the prejudices of certain people in the Chan and Pure Land schools, he wrote the famous Four Selections, in which he said:
“With Chan and with the Pure Land, like a tiger wearing horns, in this life a teacher of people, in the future a Buddha and patriarch.”
How can these patriarchs who had both Chan and Pure Land be slandered as 'impure Pure Land' and denied?!
Since Master Yongming is a manifestation of Amitabha Buddha
(Master Yongming's birthday, the seventeenth day of the eleventh lunar month, is taken as Amitabha Buddha's birthday)

, his thought is as if spoken by Amitabha Buddha himself. The successive patriarchs of the Pure Land school after Master Yongming take the Record of the Mirror of the Source as their standard and follow it, so how can one say they 'had no lineage'? This is what is meant by the dwarf spitting at the sun.
